name: Editorial grid
source: A Swiss editorial title sequence on a white canvas: hairline red rules that slide and re-divide the frame, one condensed bold red word per beat set inside a cell, photographs that live in cells and resize with them, and tiny tracked caption blocks in cell corners. Described from a contact sheet; no files or pixels are carried.

frame_device.what: A few 1 px rules (3 to 6 lines, ink or accent colour, full-bleed or stopping at a cell corner) divide the frame into uneven cells. A small square tick sits where two rules cross. Every element lives in a cell: one hero word, one image, one or two caption blocks in cell corners. Nothing floats free of the rules.
frame_device.moves: On every beat the rules slide to new positions (0.6 to 0.8 s, expo.inOut) and the cells resize with them, so the hero word, the image and the captions are carried to their new cells by the grid itself. A rule may run on from the frame edge to a point (draw-on) or retract off the edge. Between beats the grid never rests more than about 1 s.

type.classes: Hero: one condensed bold caps word (a tall grotesque, 700 to 800 weight, tight tracking), in the accent colour, sized to its cell (60 to 85% of the cell width, never the whole frame). Caption: 2 to 4 lines of tiny tracked caps (about 1.1 to 1.4% of frame height, letter-spacing 0.08em) in the accent colour, anchored to a cell corner. Optional counter: a section number in the same caption class.
type.behaviour: The hero word is always fully readable at rest and sits inside one cell with padding of at least 4% of the cell; it enters by a mask-reveal (a clip-path slide up inside the cell, 0.45 s, expo.out) or is carried in by a resizing cell, never cropped at rest. A hero that does not fit its cell makes the cell bigger, not the word smaller than the caption class. Captions type on (0.4 s, steps) or fade in 0.15 s after the cell settles, and never overlap the hero.

image.treatment: Photographs and product screens are rectangular windows that live in cells, edge to edge with the cell and framed by the rules (no shadow, no rounding). The ground around may be the same image desaturated and blurred behind the grid for variety, with the rules over it.
image.behaviour: An image grows, shrinks and moves only by its cell resizing: the window changes size while the picture inside keeps its scale (crop-reframe), then a slow 4 to 6% push-in runs inside the window. Images swap by a cell collapsing to a point and the next cell opening from it. An image never floats, rotates or overlaps a rule.

transitions: grid re-divide (rules slide to a new layout)
cell swap (a cell collapses to its corner and the next opens)
rule wipe (a rule sweeps across the frame and the new content shows behind it)
image window grows to full bleed and the rules draw back over it
hero word cell expands into the next beat's image cell
grid collapses to the end lockup's rules

techniques.name: Rule re-divide
techniques.what: All rules slide at once to a new set of positions, so every cell changes size and the content is reframed on the beat.
techniques.route: Rules are absolutely positioned 1 px divs (or SVG lines) driven by CSS variables or a GSAP tween per line, 0.7 s expo.inOut, staggered 0.04 s. Content boxes are sized from the same variables (calc on the rule positions) so they follow.

techniques.name: Rule draw-on
techniques.what: A rule grows from a frame edge or from a crossing tick to its place, drawing the layout in before the content arrives.
techniques.route: A div with transform-origin at the start and scaleX/scaleY 0 to 1 (0.5 s, power3.out), or an SVG line with stroke-dasharray/dashoffset. Ticks pop in at crossings (scale 0 to 1, 0.2 s, back.out).

techniques.name: Cell window image
techniques.what: A photograph or screen opens in a cell like a window and resizes with it, the picture keeping its scale inside.
techniques.route: A div with overflow hidden or clip-path inset() for the cell, the image absolutely positioned inside with a fixed width; animate the cell's clip-path inset and position together (0.8 s expo.inOut), plus a slow image scale 1.0 to 1.06 over the hold.

techniques.name: Hero word mask reveal
techniques.what: The hero word slides up out of a mask inside its cell, one word per beat.
techniques.route: Wrap the word in an overflow hidden line box; yPercent 105 to 0, 0.45 s expo.out. Exit by yPercent 0 to -105, 0.3 s power3.in, or let the cell carry it away.

techniques.name: Caption type-on
techniques.what: Tiny caption blocks in cell corners type in as the cell settles, a second voice under the hero.
techniques.route: Split the caption into characters (or lines) and reveal with steps: stagger 0.015 s per character, 0.4 s total, opacity 0 to 1; position by cell corner (left/bottom of the cell box).

techniques.name: Cell swap
techniques.what: One cell collapses to a point at a rule crossing and the next beat's cell opens from the same point, a cut that is a movement.
techniques.route: Animate the outgoing cell's clip-path inset to 100% on three sides toward the crossing (0.35 s power3.in) then the incoming cell from the same point (0.5 s expo.out); rules re-divide in parallel.

techniques.name: Desaturated ground
techniques.what: The same photograph fills the frame in greyscale and blur behind the grid while the colour window sits in a cell, so cell and ground read as one picture.
techniques.route: A full-frame image with filter grayscale(1) blur(14px) (skip blur on a flat film; use grayscale and an 80% white overlay instead) and the cell showing the same image in colour at the same alignment.

techniques.name: Word cell grows into the image
techniques.what: The hero word's cell expands to become the next beat's image window, so the word hands the frame to the picture.
techniques.route: Tween the cell box (left/top/width/height or clip-path) over 0.8 s expo.inOut while the word fades 0.2 s early; the image is already behind the cell with the same alignment.

techniques.name: Section counter and ticks
techniques.what: A tiny caption counts the beat (01, 02, ...) and ticks mark crossings, so the sequence has a printed rhythm.
techniques.route: A caption span whose text swaps on each beat with a 0.12 s opacity dip; tick squares are 5 px divs at rule crossings that follow the rule variables.

techniques.name: Staggered cell fill
techniques.what: Three or four cells fill in a quick order (image, word, caption) on one beat instead of all at once.
techniques.route: A GSAP timeline with stagger 0.08 s over cells; each cell reveals by clip-path inset (0.45 s expo.out); keep the order fixed across beats so the rhythm is learnable.

techniques.name: Grid becomes the lockup
techniques.what: At the end the rules settle into the end card's lines, the last cell holding the logo, with the caption block under it.
techniques.route: Final re-divide to a two-rule layout (0.9 s expo.inOut); the logo mask-reveals in its cell; captions type on last; rules hold, nothing else moves.

signature: The grid is the transition: every cut is the rules sliding to a new division, and at the end they collapse into the lockup's own rules.

density.note: A re-divide plus a new hero word, image or caption about every 1 s; hold a settled grid for no more than 0.5 s.

palette.ink: the accent itself, or near black for captions
palette.note: A brand palette overrides these; the devices stay. Images carry the only other colour.

do: Commit to 3 to 6 rules and keep them 1 px (2 px at most at 4K)
Let every element live in a cell and move only when its cell moves
One hero word per beat, always fully readable inside its cell
Re-divide the grid on the beat, with expo.inOut
Give captions to the real product: tiny tracked lines that say something true
Align every image window to the rules exactly
dont: Do not float images, rotate them or add shadows
Do not crop the hero word at rest or scale it past its cell
Do not use more than one accent colour
Do not add gradients, glow or 3D
Do not let rules overlap type
Do not leave the grid static for more than a second
